about: Quotes commonly credited to someone who, by a cited investigation, did not say or write them. Each entry names the source of that finding. The quote text is the common modern wording, one sentence, quoted to identify it. Reviewed 2026-10-25.

misattributed.quote: Everything we hear is an opinion, not a fact. Everything we see is a perspective, not the truth.
misattributed.finding: The sentence is not in the Meditations; several passages say that things are as we judge them, but none pairs opinion with perspective.

misattributed.quote: All truth passes through three stages. First, it is ridiculed. Second, it is violently opposed. Third, it is accepted as being self-evident.
misattributed.finding: Researchers have not found this adage in Schopenhauer's writings. He wrote a different remark about truth and three stages; the popular version circulated in English by 1937.

misattributed.quote: And those who were seen dancing were thought to be insane by those who could not hear the music.
misattributed.finding: No evidence that Nietzsche wrote or said it. A precursor appears in Germaine de Stael's De l'Allemagne (1813); a close modern wording is in George Carlin's Brain Droppings (1997).

misattributed.quote: The secret of change is to focus all of your energy, not on fighting the old, but on building the new.
misattributed.finding: The line is spoken by a character nicknamed Socrates in Dan Millman's Way of the Peaceful Warrior (1980), not by the Greek philosopher.

misattributed.quote: Be kind, for everyone you meet is fighting a hard battle.
misattributed.finding: The earliest known versions are by Ian Maclaren, the pen name of John Watson, in the 1890s, with "Be pitiful" in place of "Be kind".

misattributed.quote: The degree of civilization in a society can be judged by entering its prisons.
misattributed.finding: Not found in Dostoevsky's writings, including The House of the Dead; the sentence first appeared in English in the late 1960s as a prison-reform motto.
misattributed.sourceTitle: Los Angeles Review of Books, Ilya Vinitsky

misattributed.quote: Insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results.
misattributed.finding: No substantive evidence Einstein said it; the saying appears in the mid-1980s without his name, and is listed as misattributed in The Ultimate Quotable Einstein.

misattributed.quote: Everybody is a genius. But if you judge a fish by its ability to climb a tree, it will live its whole life believing that it is stupid.
misattributed.finding: No substantive evidence Einstein said it; the earliest close match credited to him is in a 2004 self-help book.

misattributed.quote: Be the change you wish to see in the world.
misattributed.finding: Not traced in Gandhi's writings; the closest documented idea is a 1913 remark about changing ourselves, and the slogan's earliest close match is from 1974.

misattributed.quote: The only thing necessary for the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing.
misattributed.finding: Not found in Burke's writings; the earliest known attribution to him is in a 1920 speech, and the original author is unknown.

misattributed.quote: If I had asked people what they wanted, they would have said faster horses.
misattributed.finding: No solid evidence Ford said it; the earliest link to his name is from 1999, decades after his death.
Written by the historian Laurel Thatcher Ulrich in a 1976 article in American Quarterly.
